items.note: Limited to 20 servings a day. Rice okayu with umeboshi, simmered shiitake, kombu, pickles, chilled tofu, ohitashi, kinpira and simmered root vegetables — plant-forward and rice-based, which is the good news. But the temple publishes NO allergen, gluten-free, vegan or shojin statement at all, the tofu arrives under a dark poured sauce (soy sauce vs tamari unstated), and the okayu/simmered dishes' dashi base is unstated. Ask dish by dish.

items.ja: 本枯節と子岩魚の出汁茶漬け
items.romaji: Honkarebushi to Ko-iwana no Dashi Chazuke
items.en: Dashi Chazuke with Aged Bonito and Juvenile Char
items.note: Do not order this one on either diet. 本枯節 is fully-cured BONITO and 子岩魚 is CHAR — the dish is fish twice over, so it is not vegan and not shojin despite the temple setting. Chazuke broth is also soy-sauce seasoned as a rule. Limited to 20 servings; the cafe's own recommendation.

items.ja: 小布施栗のちまき御膳
items.note: The better lunch bet of the two. Chimaki is glutinous RICE steamed in a bamboo leaf — naturally wheat-free — with chestnuts from Obuse. But it is a gozen (set), so the accompanying dishes are unlisted and unlabelled; the sweetening and any simmered sides are the unknowns. Ask what comes on the tray.

July–August only. Watermelon sorbet, konpeito sugar candy and a non-alcoholic drink are all fine — but the set is built around 檸檬ケーキ (lemon CAKE, i.e. wheat flour) with レモンチーズクリーム (dairy cheese cream). The sorbet and konpeito alone would work; ask whether the cake can be left off.

READ THIS BEFORE ORDERING ANY DRINK HERE: the drink menu states 「※全てお茶菓子が付きます」 — EVERY drink is served with a tea sweet, and that sweet is never named. The menu photograph shows a yellow castella-type sponge, which is a wheat cake. Matcha itself is just powdered tea and water, so ask them to hold the sweet or tell you what it is.

items.ja: ホットコーヒー　〜大勧進オリジナルブレンド〜
items.note: Black coffee is wheat-free and plant-based; the unnamed tea sweet that comes with every drink is the risk. Ask them to hold it.
Same as the hot: the coffee is fine, the compulsory unnamed tea sweet is not documented.

items.ja: 玄米珈琲（ノンカフェイン）
items.en: Brown Rice Coffee, caffeine-free (hot or iced)
items.note: Roasted brown RICE, not a grain-coffee blend with barley — the cafe markets it purely as caffeine-free and names no other grain. That makes it the most promising drink here for a celiac, but the shop confirms nothing and the tea sweet still arrives with it. Ask.

items.en: Japanese Black Tea, hot — apple / blueberry / lemon
items.note: Domestic black tea in three fruit infusions. Tea and fruit are fine; the unnamed tea sweet is the open question.
Apple soda — 'cider' here means the soft drink, not alcoholic cider. No wheat or animal ingredient in the drink itself; the tea sweet remains unlabelled.

items.ja: 信州産リンゴジュース
items.note: Straight Nagano apple juice. Safe as a liquid; ask about the tea sweet served alongside.

items.en: Herbal (Yakuzen) Craft Cola, hot or iced
items.note: Spiced medicinal-herb cola syrup. The spice blend is not published — craft cola syrups occasionally use malt, and some are honey-sweetened. Worth asking about on both counts, plus the tea sweet.

items.ja: 野草茶3種飲み比べ（ホット）
items.en: Flight of Three Japanese Wild-Herb Teas
items.note: Three wild-herb teas to compare — the historic list ran dokudami, horsetail, mugwort and loquat leaf, none of them a gluten grain (note it is not 麦茶 barley tea). Herb infusions are plant-based. The tea sweet is again the only unresolved part.

items.ja: キッシュプレートランチ
items.en: Quiche Plate Lunch (choose your quiche + deli sides + soup)
items.note: The house signature and the worst choice on a gluten-free diet: quiche is a wheat pastry shell with egg and cream. Nagano-grown vegetable sides come with it, plus chicken, gibier and beef options. Not vegan either.

items.en: Rice Plate — 24-grain rice, pick your deli sides
items.note: The best-shaped option here for a restricted diet — you pick your own sides from the 60+ item showcase, so you can steer around problems. TWO CATCHES: it is served with ナン (naan, wheat) which you should decline, and the rice is 24穀米, a 24-grain blend that in Japan almost always contains BARLEY (押麦/もち麦) and sometimes wheat. Ask for plain white or brown rice instead — the kitchen also stocks 長野県産玄米.

items.en: Muffin Plate (muffin, cookie, salad, soup, deli sides)
items.note: Built on a wheat-flour muffin baked fresh each morning, with a cookie alongside. Wheat, egg and dairy.

items.ja: 長野県産鹿肉の低温調理
items.note: The house is a gibier specialist and this is its purest expression — sous-vide Nagano venison, which the shop promotes as high-protein and low-calorie. Plain cooked meat has no wheat in it, but the marinade or finishing sauce is not published; venison is very often soy-marinated. Sold from the showcase without a listed price.

items.ja: ブロッコリーのアーリオ・オーリオ
items.en: Broccoli in Garlic and Olive Oil
items.note: Garlic, olive oil, chilli and broccoli — one of the very few things in this wheat-heavy deli that is naturally free of both gluten and animal products. Note a near-identical dish on the party menu adds mozzarella and shio-koji, so specify the plain aglio e olio version.

Okinawan shredded carrot — the classic version is bound with EGG and seasoned with dashi and soy sauce, so treat it as containing egg, fish and wheat until the kitchen says otherwise. Appears in the deli case and across the bento menus.

items.ja: レッドキャベツのラペサラダ
items.note: A French-style raw slaw — usually just vinegar, oil and salt, which would make it both GF and vegan, but 'rapée' salads are sometimes bound with mayonnaise (egg). Ask. A carrot-and-fig version is also in rotation.

items.ja: 信州きのこのバルサミコマリネ
items.note: Local mushrooms in balsamic vinegar and oil — plant-based, and balsamic is grape-derived rather than grain-derived, so this is a good candidate. Confirm no soy sauce was added to the marinade.

items.ja: ブロッコリーと長芋のサブジ
items.en: Broccoli and Yam Sabzi (Indian dry curry)
items.note: Indian-style dry-spiced vegetables. Sabzi is normally whole spices, oil and vegetables with no wheat and no dairy — but ghee and yoghurt are common in Japanese kitchens' versions. Ask about both.
Whole roasted onion — about as simple and as safe as this showcase gets on both diets. Still worth confirming no butter or stock was used in the roasting.

items.ja: 豆富のハンバーグ ピザ職人風
items.note: A tofu patty rather than a meat one, but 'pizzaiolo style' means a tomato-and-cheese finish, so expect DAIRY. Japanese hamburg patties are also routinely bound with panko (wheat) and egg. Not the vegan option it looks like.

items.ja: カリフラワーと大豆ミートのヘルシーオムレツ
items.romaji: Cauliflower to Daizu Meat no Healthy Omelette
items.note: Soy meat sounds promising but it is set in an OMELETTE — egg, so not vegan. Textured soy protein is also frequently wheat-extended; ask if gluten matters.

items.ja: 全粒粉入り韓国風ちぢみ
items.note: The shop names the flour itself — 全粒粉, WHOLEMEAL WHEAT. Chijimi batter also normally contains egg and the dipping sauce is soy-based. Named here so it is clearly flagged rather than mistaken for a rice pancake.

items.ja: 海老入り水餃子 鶏白湯スープ
items.en: Prawn Dumplings in Chicken Paitan Soup
items.note: Gyoza wrappers are wheat and the broth is chicken. Listed so it is unambiguous.

items.section: 前菜＆ジビエソーセージ (Tapas & Gibier Sausage, dinner)
items.note: The house identity dish — badger, wild boar and deer. Sausages routinely carry wheat rusk or wheat starch as a binder and the shop publishes no ingredient list, so ask the kitchen about the filler. Singles are also sold: 穴熊 badger ¥480, 猪 wild boar ¥480, 鹿 deer ¥580, 鹿ノワール ¥680.

items.ja: フレンチフライ　ワカモーレ
items.section: 前菜＆ジビエソーセージ (Tapas, dinner)
items.note: Potato and avocado are both fine in principle, and this is one of the few dinner plates with no obvious wheat. The problems are the shared FRYER (this kitchen deep-fries aji-fry, fritto misto and fish and chips in it) and whether the guacamole contains dairy. Ask about both.

items.ja: タンドリーチキンの唐揚げ
items.section: 前菜＆ジビエソーセージ (Tapas, dinner)
items.note: Karaage means a flour/starch dredge and a deep fry — the shop does not state the flour, and karaage marinades are soy-based. Tandoori marinade is also yoghurt-based. Assume wheat.

items.section: 前菜＆ジビエソーセージ (Tapas, dinner)
items.note: ¥750 for three kinds, ¥1,180 for five. Dairy — vegetarian but not vegan. The cheese is wheat-free; ask them to hold any crackers or bread served with it.
The dairy-free coffee here. Espresso and soy milk, nothing else.

items.ja: レインフォレスト認証 オーガニックコーヒー
items.note: Organic Honduran beans. Black coffee — no wheat, no animal products. A house-roasted single origin is also offered at ¥600.
Herbal infusion — no gluten grain, no animal ingredient. Chinese tea (¥550) and plain black tea (¥550) are equally straightforward.
Kurozu is brewed from brown RICE, not barley — unusual among vinegars in being reliably gluten-free. Non-alcoholic and plant-based.

items.ja: 自家製ジンジャーエール
items.note: House ginger syrup with soda. No wheat, but house ginger syrups are sometimes sweetened with HONEY — ask if you are strict vegan.

items.en: 100% Juice — mango, apple, cranberry, guava, orange, grapefruit, grape or tomato
items.note: Eight straight juices, all ¥500. The simplest safe order in the building. Note the shop charges a ¥350 table charge if you order only à la carte, and a one-drink minimum outside lunch and course bookings.

items.en: Shiga Kogen Beer (Nagano craft — pale ale, IPA, saison, porter, blonde)
items.note: Six Nagano craft beers at ¥820 each. All brewed from malted barley and/or wheat — contains gluten. No gluten-free beer is stocked; the alcohol-free Suntory All-Free (¥450) is also a barley-malt product and is NOT gluten-free either.

items.ja: ご飯プレート（テイクアウト弁当）
items.en: Rice Plate Takeout Bento — curry or gapao, rotating
items.note: ¥1,280 list, discounted to ¥1,080. Rotates through Ueda venison tomato curry, gapao rice, red / green / yellow / spinach curries. Thai curries here mean fish sauce and shrimp paste, and gapao is oyster- and soy-sauce seasoned — so not vegan and not reliably wheat-free. The 24-grain rice barley caveat applies to the Variety BOX (¥1,200) too.

items.section: 接待弁当 (Premium bento, order ahead)
items.note: Listed at ¥1,500 BEFORE tax. Chapchae, chicken piccata, potato salad, prawn-celery marinade, Nagano brown rice, 24-grain rice with house achar, seasonal chiffon cake. Contains egg and dairy; the chiffon cake is wheat and the 24-grain rice likely contains barley. Larger tiers run ¥2,000 / ¥2,500 / ¥3,000 before tax. Ordering ahead is the point — the shop's own line is 「アレルギーをお持ちのお客様は、ご予約して頂くことを強くおすすめしております」, and for parties 「アレルギーや好き嫌いがございましたらお知らせください」. Book and declare.

items.en: Oyaki filled with Nozawana Pickled Greens
items.note: NOT GLUTEN-FREE on two counts. Oyaki dough is wheat flour, and this shop's defining trait is that it DEEP-FRIES its oyaki rather than steaming them — so there is a shared fryer on top of the wheat. Nozawana filling is conventionally seasoned with soy sauce and often bonito flakes; the shop publishes nothing, so vegan is unverifiable.
NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. Eggplant oyaki filling is conventionally miso-based, and neither the miso type nor whether dashi is in it is stated anywhere.

items.en: Oyaki filled with Broad-Bean Sweet Paste
items.note: NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. A sweet bean paste filling is the most likely of the seven to be plant-only, but with no ingredient statement and a shared fryer, nothing is confirmed.

items.en: Oyaki filled with Chunky Red Bean Paste
items.note: NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. Price read off the shop's in-store hanging price board in 2021; the three flavours with newer data have since risen about ¥20, so expect ¥130 or so now.
NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. 2021 price-board figure; add roughly ¥20. Potato filling seasoning is unstated (butter and soy sauce are both common).
NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. 2021 price-board figure; add roughly ¥20. Nira fillings are usually miso- or soy-seasoned.

NOT GLUTEN-FREE — deep-fried wheat dough. 2021 price-board figure; add roughly ¥20. PRACTICAL NOTE: this is a tiny takeout-only shop at Inaba-Hizume, about 2.5 km from Nagano Station (not walkable from it), open 9:30 until sold out, and it genuinely does sell out — phone 026-221-3148 to reserve. Closed 1st/3rd/5th Sundays and 2nd/4th Mondays.
